details:
**Shortest-serving UK Prime Minister**
Truss became Prime Minister in September 2022 after winning the Conservative leadership contest to replace Boris Johnson. She resigned after only about seven weeks, making her the shortest-serving prime minister in British history.

**Rishi Sunak**
Truss's rival in the 2022 Conservative leadership race, whom she defeated in the members' vote. After her resignation in October 2022, Sunak succeeded her as Prime Minister.

**The lettuce**
The British tabloid the Daily Star ran a livestream of a head of iceberg lettuce to see whether it would outlast Truss's premiership. The lettuce "won" when Truss resigned, and it became the defining joke about her time in office.

**Mini-budget**
The September 2022 fiscal plan announced by her Chancellor, Kwasi Kwarteng, which included large unfunded tax cuts. It caused the pound to crash and turmoil in the bond markets, forcing the Bank of England to step in. Truss fired Kwarteng and replaced him with Jeremy Hunt, who reversed most of the plan.

**Energy Price Guarantee**
Truss's policy capping household energy prices in response to soaring gas prices after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. It was announced to last two years, but Jeremy Hunt cut it back to six months.

**Suella Braverman's resignation letter**
Braverman resigned as Truss's Home Secretary in October 2022, officially for sending a government document from her personal email. Her letter openly criticized the government, saying that "pretending we haven't made mistakes" and "hoping that things will magically come right" was not serious politics. Truss resigned the next day.

**"The Iron Weathercock"**
A mocking nickname for Truss that played on Margaret Thatcher's nickname "The Iron Lady" and referred to her many changes of position, including moving from campaigning for the Liberal Democrats and backing Remain to becoming a Conservative Brexit supporter.

**Fullbrook Strategies**
The lobbying firm of Mark Fullbrook, Truss's Downing Street chief of staff. It was reported that he was paid through the firm rather than as a regular civil servant, which raised questions about tax and conflicts of interest.

**Queen Elizabeth II's last prime minister**
Truss was appointed by Queen Elizabeth II at Balmoral Castle on September 6, 2022, two days before the Queen died. She was the last of the fifteen prime ministers appointed during the Queen's reign.

**Foreign Secretary under Boris Johnson**
Before becoming Prime Minister, Truss served as Foreign Secretary in Boris Johnson's government from 2021 to 2022, after earlier cabinet posts including International Trade Secretary.
